subject: Order Form redlines — output ownership & training/feedback license (proposal)
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@horizondatainc.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form redlines — output ownership & training rights

Hi Chloe,

Attached is our redlined order form and a short cover note from our legal team. Two items are blocking procurement on our side and we'd like to resolve them this week if possible:

1) Output ownership: Our legal team wants explicit language that HorizonData retains ownership of customer-provided data and of "Outputs" (definitions included in the redline). We understand Redwood's standard terms say outputs are licensed — we need clarity on whether your standard grants any rights to use customer outputs beyond delivering the service (particularly for model training).

2) Training / feedback license: The attached redline proposes a complete carve-out: Redwood may not use any Customer Data or Outputs to train or improve models unless HorizonData expressly opts in via a separate agreement. We are open to limited telemetry/aggregation but not raw output reuse.

Can your team confirm what you can accept? If helpful, we can hop on a 30-minute sync today.

Attachments: Horizon_OrderForm_redline.docx (document/x-docx), redlines_summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Alice Park
Senior Counsel, HorizonData Inc
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@horizondatainc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — output ownership & training rights

Alice — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the redlines. Looping in our legal and sales leads so we can move quickly.

Quick internal summary for context:
- Business: we generally allow customers to retain ownership of their inputs and outputs; our standard order form grants a limited license to operate and improve service quality, but that language is often the friction point.
- Legal ask: HorizonData is asking for an opt-out of training (no use of outputs/customer data for model training without explicit opt-in).

Priyom — can you propose language that preserves Redwood's ability to use aggregated telemetry for service improvement while protecting HorizonData's Outputs from being used to train public models? We want something that legal can agree to and sales can live with operationally.

Aditya — if we can offer an explicit opt-in for training at the order form level (or a separate appendix), would that unblock procurement?

Alice — happy to set a 30 minute call today (I have availability 2–4pm PT).

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@horizondatainc.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — proposed clause options

Chloe / team / Alice,

Thanks for the ping — reviewed HorizonData's redline. Below are two pragmatic options (keeps negotiation tight, avoids broad license grants):

Option A (Customer-friendly, stricter):
"Customer Data and Customer Outputs (collectively, \"Customer Content\") are and will remain the sole property of Customer. Except as required to provide the Service to Customer, Redwood shall not use, sell, license, distribute, or otherwise exploit Customer Content for any purpose, including training or improving any models, without Customer's prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry that cannot be reverse-engineered to identify Customer or Customer Content for the sole purpose of measuring and improving service metrics (e.g., latency, errors)."

Option B (Operational compromise):
"Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer Outputs. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use Customer Content solely to provide and improve the Service (including model quality improvements). Such license does not permit use of Customer Content to train publicly available foundation models. Redwood may, however, use de-identified and aggregated derivatives of Customer Content for internal model tuning and service optimizations, provided that such derivatives cannot be reconstituted to reveal Customer Content and are not used to train models that will be made generally available without Customer's consent. Customers may opt out of any such internal tuning via an explicit checkbox or appendix to the Order Form."

Key guidance: Option A will likely require a price premium or specific assurance operationally (we'd need to implement separate product flags to respect opt-outs). Option B gives us flexibility to iterate and reduce cost while giving the customer an opt-out path.

Attached is a short plain-text snippet you can drop into the order form: proposed_feedback_clause.txt

Happy to join a call to walk Alice through the differences.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@horizondatainc.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T08:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — confirmation and next steps

Alice — thanks for the patience. From a commercial standpoint, we can accept Option B (the operational compromise) with the following practical commitments:
- We will add an Order Form appendix that makes the internal-tuning/opt-out explicit (checkbox in procurement UI + clause in order form).
- We will not use Customer Outputs to train any public models without separate written opt-in.
- If HorizonData opts out, we'll raise a modest charge to account for lost optimization benefits; we can discuss numbers after legal agrees to text.

If that sounds acceptable, can you confirm and we'll prepare a clean order form + DocuSign today? Chloe / Priyom will produce the exact clause for insertion.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
From: Samuel Ortiz <sam.ortiz@horizondatainc.com>

Aditya / Chloe / Priyom — thanks, this addresses our core concerns. HorizonData is willing to accept Option B with the opt-out appendix and the assurance that Outputs will not be used to train public models without an opt-in. Procurement asks that the opt-out be clearly visible on the order form and that any price delta for opting out be disclosed before signature.

Please send a clean order form and the DocuSign link; procurement is ready to sign once the appendix is in place and the delta is called out.
